ing: 15 oz each, drained, or 1.5 cups dried fava beans cooked until tender
st: Pour the beans and their liquid into a medium pot with the water. If you used dried beans, use their cooking liquid instead.
Heat over medium until the beans simmer, then cook for 10 minutes until very hot and soft.
Mash about half the beans with a fork or masher, leaving the rest whole for texture.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, salt and pepper and cook 3 minutes.
Remove from the heat and stir in the lemon juice and [[2 tbsp]] olive oil.
Taste and adjust the salt and lemon.
Spoon into bowls and top with the tomatoes, feta and parsley. Drizzle with the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Serve with warm flatbread for scooping.
Whisk the sorghum flour, wheat flour, yeast and salt in a large bowl.
Add [[3 cups]] warm water and whisk into a smooth, thin batter with no lumps.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 8 hours or overnight so it ferments and smells pleasantly sour. It should be bubbly.
Stir the batter. If it is thicker than crepe batter, thin it with water, up to [[0.5 cup]].
Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium heat and wipe it lightly with oil.
Pour in a ladle of batter and spread it very thin by tilting the pan. Cook for 2 minutes until dry on top and the edges lift.
Do not flip. Lift the flatbread off carefully and stack on a plate under a cloth to stay soft.
Repeat with the remaining batter, oiling the pan between batches. Serve with stews.

ing: or use cornmeal or wheat flour
trimmed, cooked in a stew for serving
st: Bring [[3 cups]] water and the salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Whisk [[1 cup]] sorghum flour into [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth and pour into the boiling water, stirring constantly.
Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thickened.
Lower the heat. Add the rest of the flour gradually, stirring hard with a wooden spoon so no lumps form.
Cook, stirring and pressing the dough against the pot, for 8 minutes until stiff, smooth and shiny.
Wet a bowl, scoop in the asida and swirl it to form a smooth dome. Turn out onto a plate.
Make a dent in the top. Pour in the melted butter.
Serve with the yogurt and a stew of okra on the side, eating by scooping with the fingers.
If using dried okra, rinse it and soak in warm water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 8 minutes.
Add the onions and cook for 6 minutes until soft and golden.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, coriander, cumin, salt and pepper. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add [[4 cups]] water. Cover and simmer for 1 hour until the beef is tender.
Add the okra and [[1 cup]] more water. Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes until the okra is soft and the stew is thick and slightly slippery.
Taste and adjust the salt. Serve with asida, kisra or rice.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and [[2 tbsp]] oil. Stir to make a soft dough.
Knead for 8 minutes on a floured counter until smooth and elastic.
Cover the bowl and let the dough rise in a warm spot until doubled.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and let them rest for 15 minutes.
Roll each ball into a round about 1/2 inch thick.
Heat a heavy skillet over medium heat and brush lightly with oil.
Cook each gurasa for 3 minutes per side, until puffed and speckled with brown. Cover the pan for the first minute to cook the inside.
Brush with a little oil and stack under a cloth to stay soft. Serve with stews or beans.
The traditional dish is eaten raw, but this home version cooks the liver fully for safety. Trim the liver of membranes and chop it into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook the liver, stirring, for 6 minutes until no pink remains and it is cooked through to at least 160°F/71°C.
Transfer to a bowl and let it cool for 5 minutes.
Stir in the onion, chilies, salt and cumin.
Whisk the peanut butter with the lemon juice and [[2 tbsp]] warm water until smooth, then mix it in.
Taste and add more salt or lemon.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve with flatbread.
Pat the lamb dry and season with the salt, pepper and cumin.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large skillet over high heat.
Add the lamb in a single layer, in two batches if needed, and sear without stirring for 3 minutes per side until browned.
Lower the heat to medium and cover for 12 minutes, until the lamb is tender and cooked through to at least 145°F/63°C.
Move the lamb to a plate. Add the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil and cook the onions for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and chili and cook for 1 minute.
Return the lamb to the pan and toss for 2 minutes. Serve hot with flatbread and lemon wedges.

ing: medium, cut into rounds or cubes
st: Sprinkle the eggplant with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and leave in a colander for 15 minutes to draw out bitterness. Pat dry.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Fry the eggplant in batches for 4 minutes per side until deeply browned and soft. Drain on paper towels.
In a bowl, whisk the peanut butter, lemon juice, garlic, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the warm water until smooth and pourable.
Place the eggplant in a serving dish, with the tomato if using.
Pour the peanut dressing over the eggplant and toss gently.
Sprinkle with parsley. Serve warm or at room temperature with bread.

ing: melted, plus more for the pan
st: Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and grease a 9 by 13-inch baking pan with butter.
Mix the semolina, [[0.75 cup]] sugar, coconut and baking powder in a bowl.
Add the yogurt, melted butter and vanilla and stir to a thick batter. Rest it for 15 minutes so the semolina softens.
Spread the batter in the pan and smooth the top. Cut into diamonds or squares with a knife and press an almond into each.
Bake for 30 minutes until golden brown on top.
Meanwhile, simmer [[1.5 cups]] sugar, [[1 cup]] water and the lemon juice for 8 minutes. Cool the syrup to room temperature.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot cake right when it comes out of the oven, so it soaks in.
Let it cool for 20 minutes before serving.
Rinse the dried hibiscus flowers under cold water.
Bring [[6 cups]] water to a boil in a pot.
Add the hibiscus, remove from the heat and cover.
Steep for 15 minutes, until the liquid is a deep ruby red.
Strain into a pitcher, pressing the flowers to get all the color out.
Stir in the sugar until it dissolves, then add the lime juice.
Add the mint. Serve hot, or chill and pour over ice. Taste and add more sugar if too tart.
